events.symbol_or_condition: pcap_set_snaplen or pcap_set_promisc or pcap_set_timeout or pcap_set_immediate_mode or pcap_set_buffer_size
pcap_compile; transition tracked for the struct bpf_program resource while the associated pcap_t active-state requirement is a precondition
pcap_setfilter; capture-handle state is tracked while valid compiled-program state is a separate resource precondition
enclosing fuzz-driver function return or exit

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Successful creation acquires a pcap_t that remains caller-owned until pcap_close.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: A non-NULL return from pcap_create must establish UNACTIVATED_OWNED before the acquired pcap_t is used.
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: API_CALL:any modeled pcap_t operation requiring an acquired handle

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: A failed create does not establish the successful-handle pcap_close cleanup obligation.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_create returning NULL leaves NO_HANDLE; the failed acquisition result is not a usable capture handle.
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: API_CALL:modeled pcap_t use after pcap_create failure

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Configuration does not release the acquired handle; eventual pcap_close remains required.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_set_snaplen, pcap_set_promisc, pcap_set_timeout, pcap_set_immediate_mode, and pcap_set_buffer_size require UNACTIVATED_OWNED. Calling them after activation is an ordering violation.
obligations.return_predicate: valid pre-activation configuration return == 0; an activated handle yields PCAP_ERROR_ACTIVATED where documented

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Activation does not transfer ownership. The acquired handle still requires pcap_close.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_activate is modeled from UNACTIVATED_OWNED. Reactivation of an already ACTIVE_OWNED handle is invalid.
obligations.return_predicate: return >= 0 establishes ACTIVE_OWNED; return < 0 establishes ACTIVATION_FAILED_OWNED

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: The failed-activation handle remains owned and must be closed with pcap_close.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: ACTIVATION_FAILED_OWNED is not an active-use state. After a negative pcap_activate result, active-only operations are not permitted.

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Caller is responsible for pcap_close after successful creation, including pre-activation exits and activation-failure exits.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: Every non-NULL pcap_create acquisition must reach CLOSED through pcap_close on every relevant normal or error exit.

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Cleanup must be guarded by successful handle acquisition and must not be omitted merely because activation failed.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_close cleanup is tied to a currently acquired UNACTIVATED_OWNED, ACTIVE_OWNED, or ACTIVATION_FAILED_OWNED handle; pcap_create returning NULL creates no successful-handle cleanup obligation.

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: pcap_close releases the current pcap_t resource; later reuse requires a fresh logical acquisition.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: CLOSED is not a live capture-handle state. A fresh pcap_create acquisition is required for a new logical resource instance.
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: API_CALL:stateful modeled pcap_t operation after pcap_close

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Exactly one release is required for each currently-live pcap_t acquisition.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_close requires a currently owned capture handle. A second pcap_close after CLOSED is invalid.

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: The metadata query does not release capture-handle ownership.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_datalink requires ACTIVE_OWNED; a handle created by pcap_create but not yet successfully activated is not a valid pre-state.

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: The pcap_t remains caller-owned until pcap_close. A return of 1 additionally yields library-owned borrowed header/data values.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_next_ex requires an ACTIVE_OWNED live-capture handle in this scenario-bounded specification.

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Caller may inspect or copy the values but does not own their storage.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: The struct pcap_pkthdr and packet-data pointers yielded by a successful pcap_next_ex are library-owned borrowed values and must not be freed by the caller.
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: CALLER_DEALLOCATION:pcap_next_ex returned packet header or packet data

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Copy data that must outlive the documented borrowed-value lifetime.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: A borrowed header/data view is not guaranteed to remain valid after the next packet-reading call. For this frozen V1 scope, a later pcap_next_ex invalidates reliance on the prior borrowed view unless it was copied.
obligations.return_predicate: prior borrow was not copied before subsequent packet-read call
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: USE:prior pcap_next_ex packet header or data after a subsequent in-scope pcap_next_ex call

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Successful compilation creates caller-owned compiled program state requiring eventual pcap_freecode.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_compile requires the associated pcap_t to be ACTIVE_OWNED. For a fresh BPF logical resource instance, the destination program state is NO_VALID_PROGRAM before compilation.
obligations.return_predicate: associated handle ACTIVE_OWNED; return == 0 acquires COMPILED_OWNED

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Caller is responsible for pcap_freecode for every successfully compiled program.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: Each pcap_compile return == 0 creates COMPILED_OWNED state that must reach FREED_OR_EMPTY through pcap_freecode on every relevant exit.

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Guard successful-program use and cleanup on pcap_compile return == 0.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: A failed pcap_compile from a fresh NO_VALID_PROGRAM resource does not create a new valid compiled program or the successful-compile cleanup obligation.
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: API_CALL:pcap_freecode or pcap_setfilter conditioned on pcap_compile result

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Filter installation does not release either the capture handle or caller-owned compiled-program cleanup duty.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: pcap_setfilter requires an ACTIVE_OWNED capture handle and a valid COMPILED_OWNED bpf_program.
obligations.return_predicate: associated pcap_t is ACTIVE_OWNED and associated bpf_program is COMPILED_OWNED

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: The caller retains the eventual pcap_freecode obligation whether pcap_setfilter succeeds or fails.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: Passing a valid compiled program to pcap_setfilter does not transfer caller ownership of the bpf_program.
obligations.return_predicate: program was successfully produced by pcap_compile
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: API_CALL:pcap_setfilter followed by later program cleanup

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: A later compilation, if desired, begins a fresh logical BPF resource lifecycle; this V1 does not infer reuse without a fresh successful compile.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: FREED_OR_EMPTY is not COMPILED_OWNED. A program whose compiled storage has been released cannot be treated as a live compiled filter program.
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: API_CALL:pcap_setfilter or other modeled live-program use after pcap_freecode

obligations.cleanup_responsibility: Apply pcap_close and pcap_freecode independently to each owned resource on all relevant exits.
obligations.required_pre_state_or_exit_condition: Each successfully acquired pcap_t and each successfully compiled bpf_program is tracked by resource identity. Cleanup of one resource does not discharge the cleanup obligation of another independent resource.
obligations.return_predicate: cleanup is conditioned on the corresponding resource's own successful acquisition
obligations.triggering_event_or_function_exit: FUNCTION_EXIT or cleanup branch involving pcap_t and/or bpf_program resources

transitions.return_predicate: pcap_activate return >= 0; zero is success and positive values are warnings
call is made on an activated handle; query does not release handle ownership
pcap_next_ex return != 1; no new packet/header borrow is created by this call and the pcap_t remains caller-owned until pcap_close
associated pcap_t is ACTIVE_OWNED and pcap_compile return == 0
associated pcap_t is ACTIVE_OWNED and pcap_compile return != 0; no new valid compiled program is acquired
associated bpf_program is COMPILED_OWNED; pcap_setfilter does not release pcap_t ownership or transfer caller ownership of the program
successful compiled-program ownership is currently live
same still-live struct bpf_program was previously normalized by pcap_freecode; pinned implementation has bf_len == 0 and bf_insns == NULL
corresponding acquired pcap_t is currently caller-owned

defect_taxonomy.D2: Use after failed initialization or activation
defect_taxonomy.D3: Use after close, destroy, end, or release
defect_taxonomy.D4: Double close, destroy, end, or release
defect_taxonomy.D5: Missing cleanup on a success or failure exit
defect_taxonomy.D6: Invalid API call ordering or missing prerequisite call
defect_taxonomy.D7: Ownership misuse: freeing borrowed data, failing transferred ownership, or wrong owner
defect_taxonomy.D8: Conditionally invalid cleanup or cleanup under the wrong state or return condition

explicit_unsupported_or_out_of_scope_con: The functions frozen in config/annotation/libpcap_v1_authoring_scope.v1.json under explicitly_excluded_functions are outside this scenario-bounded V1 modeled API set.
pcap_open_live and the offline/dead-handle families are not silently treated as equivalent to the modeled pcap_create plus pcap_activate lifecycle.
pcap_next, pcap_dispatch, pcap_loop, and pcap_breakloop are outside V1; the borrowed-value lifetime rule is instantiated only for the later in-scope pcap_next_ex call.
pcap_snapshot is outside V1; the frozen scenario phrase snapshot-length is represented by pcap_set_snaplen.
Timestamp, statistics, non-blocking, injection, dumper, device-discovery, and datalink-mutation APIs remain outside this V1 model.
No same-handle identity coupling between the pcap_t used for pcap_compile and a later pcap_setfilter call is invented beyond the frozen scope.
Reuse of a previously freed bpf_program as a fresh compile destination is not inferred as a transition in this V1; a fresh logical lifecycle must be established before such reuse is claimed valid.
General packet-processing correctness, arbitrary C bugs, buffer errors, network behavior, and memory-safety defects outside explicit protocol obligations are not classified by this specification.
Absence of a transition in this partial relation does not silently imply either validity or violation.

bpf_program_lifecycle.repeated_freecode_interpretation: T13 applies only to the same still-live struct bpf_program object after the pinned pcap_freecode implementation has normalized bf_len to zero and bf_insns to NULL. It does not authorize use of the released program as COMPILED_OWNED.

dual_resource_initial_state_representati.interpretation: The protocol schema exposes one required top-level initial_state. The V1 resource family contains two independently tracked logical resource kinds. NO_HANDLE is the schema-level default because every frozen scenario begins its capture lifecycle with pcap_create. A fresh struct bpf_program logical resource begins locally in NO_VALID_PROGRAM when pcap_compile is analyzed. This representation must be explicitly accepted or rejected by the reviewer.

resource_instance_lifecycle.ACTIVATION_FAILED_OWNED: Still-owned handle state requiring pcap_close; not an active-use state.
resource_instance_lifecycle.CLOSED: Terminal for the current pcap_t logical resource instance; later pcap_create begins a fresh instance.
resource_instance_lifecycle.FREED_OR_EMPTY: No live compiled-program ownership remains. A later successful compile, if modeled in a future lifecycle, is a fresh logical BPF resource instance.
